symptom: An @Aspect bean declared by a @Bean method that returns null (to enable the aspect conditionally) causes AopInvocationException with "object is not an instance of declaring class" when an advised method is invoked. If the aspect implements Ordered, context startup instead fails with a ClassCastException from NullBean to Ordered.
cause: A null @Bean result is registered as a NullBean placeholder, but the aspect metadata is prepared eagerly from the declared type, so advice invocation and getOrder() operate on the NullBean instead of the aspect class.
fixSummary: Spring Framework 6.2.9 skips a null aspect bean instance in AbstractAspectJAdvice and refines getOrder(), so a null @Aspect bean is tolerated. Maintainers also recommend @Conditional (or programmatic bean registration in 7.0) instead of returning null from a @Bean method.
notes: Fix version taken from the issue milestone (6.2.9); the thread describes the change in prose only.

symptom: Launching several jobs concurrently with the MongoDB job repository fails with DataIntegrityViolationException wrapping MongoDB error 112 (WriteConflict, TransientTransactionError) inside MongoSequenceIncrementer.nextLongValue().
cause: Concurrent threads increment the same sequence document in findAndModify, which produces transient write conflicts on MongoDB.

title: JsonParser.currentValue() returns a nested creator value instead of the enclosing bean in a custom deserializer (Jackson 3)
errorSample:
Caused by: java.lang.ClassCastException: class com.example.entities.SourceSystem cannot be cast to class com.example.entities.Project (com.example.entities.SourceSystem and com.example.entities.Project are in unnamed module of loader 'app')
	at com.example.entities.AssetDeserializer.deserialize(AssetDeserializer.java:19)
	at com.example.entities.AssetDeserializer.deserialize(AssetDeserializer.java:13)
	at tools.jackson.databind.deser.impl.MethodProperty.deserializeAndSet(MethodProperty.java:120)
	at tools.jackson.databind.deser.bean.BeanDeserializer.deserializeFromObject(BeanDeserializer.java:652)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A custom property deserializer that casts p.currentValue() to the enclosing bean throws ClassCastException because currentValue() is the value of an earlier nested object (here SourceSystem instead of Project). It only happens when -parameters is enabled (so constructors are auto-detected) and a nested type has a public all-args constructor.
cause: With constructor (property-based creator) deserialization the content is buffered and the bean cannot exist before its creator arguments are read, and in Jackson 3 the property-based creator overwrote the enclosing value on the parser. The enclosing instance is not generally available as currentValue() while a creator property is deserialized.
fixSummary: Fixed in Jackson 3.2.0 (property-based creator no longer clobbers the enclosing value's currentValue()). As an interim workaround the maintainer suggested disabling constructor detection with @JsonCreator(mode = DISABLED) or making the constructor non-public.
notes: Reporter's original package name was replaced with com.example in the excerpt.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Calling parser.readValueAs(new TypeReference<Map<String,String>>(){}) on a freshly created JsonParser fails in Jackson 3.0.0 with MismatchedInputException "Unexpected end-of-input", while Jackson 2.20 worked.
cause: In Jackson 3 JsonParser.readValueAs() does not advance a fresh parser to its first token (Jackson 2 did this in ObjectMapper._initForReading), so the deserializer sees no current token.
fixSummary: Fixed in Jackson 3.0.1. Workarounds: call parser.nextToken() first when currentToken() is null, or use jsonMapper.readValue(parser, type) instead of parser.readValueAs(type).

symptom: Code compiled by javac 26 with Lombok 1.18.46 fails at runtime with NoClassDefFoundError: lombok/Lombok where @SneakyThrows is used, although Lombok is documented to leave no runtime dependency. JDK 25 was fine.
cause: Lombok removes the call to Lombok.sneakyThrow in a post-compile bytecode step by wrapping the compiler's ClassWriter file manager, which relies on modifying a final field; JDK 26 starts restricting modification of final fields, so the step silently stopped running.
fixSummary: Fixed in Lombok (available first in the edge release, shipped in v1.18.48 per the issue milestone).
notes: Reporter's workaround is not given in the thread; the fix was confirmed with the edge release. Release 1.18.48 is taken from the milestone.

title: classpath*: resource scanning misses jars on java.class.path whose directory contains % (or throws "Malformed escape pair")
errorSample:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Malformed escape pair: /…/repro/lib/100%/demo.jar
	at java.base/sun.net.www.ParseUtil.decode(ParseUtil.java:207)
	at java.base/sun.net.www.protocol.file.Handler.openConnection(Handler.java:69)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver silently omits jars from classpath*: results when a directory in java.class.path contains a percent-encoded-looking sequence (e.g. host%3A8099), and throws IllegalArgumentException "Malformed escape pair" when the directory contains a bare % (e.g. 100%).
cause: ClassPathManifestEntry.fixPath escapes # but not %, and asJarFileResource builds a jar:file: URL from the raw path, so opening the URL decodes % sequences again and points at a different (non-existent) file.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Framework 7.0.10. The maintainer's approach checks whether the resource exists and, if not, retries with % escaped as %25, so both pre-encoded and literal % paths keep working.
notes: The reporter first proposed always escaping %; the maintainer pointed out that would drop support for pre-encoded class path entries, hence the existence-check approach. Fix version from the milestone.

symptom: A @Valid request body with a large byte[] field that violates @Size (6 MB with -Xmx256m) causes OutOfMemoryError during exception handling instead of a normal validation error response.
cause: The exception message of MethodArgumentNotValidException includes FieldError.toString(), which uses ObjectUtils.nullSafeToString on the rejected byte[] value; that formats each byte through a StringJoiner and needs roughly 48 bytes of heap per byte (about 288 MB for 6 MB).

symptom: A repository method returning a single interface projection from a multi-field JPQL @Query fails with ConversionFailedException (Object[] to the projection interface), while the same query returning a List works. It only occurs with EclipseLink 5.0.0, not Hibernate.

symptom: JdbcTemplate.batchUpdate against Sybase ASE (jConnect) throws TransientDataAccessResourceException for a duplicate-key insert instead of DuplicateKeyException.
cause: SQLStateSQLExceptionTranslator (the default translator when no sql-error-codes mapping applies) looks only at the outer BatchUpdateException and does not unwrap it to the next exception in the chain, unlike SQLErrorCodeSQLExceptionTranslator which was the default up to 5.3.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Framework 6.2.12 so BatchUpdateException is unwrapped in SQLStateSQLExceptionTranslator and SQLExceptionSubclassTranslator. Earlier workaround: force SQLErrorCodeSQLExceptionTranslator by putting an (even empty) sql-error-codes.xml at the classpath root or configuring it on the JdbcTemplate.

title: Non-deterministic IllegalStateException "Body token not expected" in PartGenerator when reading multipart file parts
errorSample:
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Body token not expected
        at org.springframework.http.codec.multipart.PartGenerator$CreateFileState.body(PartGenerator.java:457)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Parsing a multipart/form-data response with WebClient (bodyToFlux(Part.class)) intermittently fails with IllegalStateException "Body token not expected" from PartGenerator$CreateFileState.body.
cause: PartGenerator requests additional tokens while it is still busy creating the temporary file in CreateFileState; if file creation takes long enough, a new body token arrives in a state that only expects the file-creation result.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Framework 7.0.8 (issue is marked as backported); the maintainer also fixed related resource-cleanup problems in the same code.
notes: Cause is from the maintainer's comment; the exact 6.2.x release carrying the backport is not stated in the thread. The reporter observed it only with file parts larger than maxInMemorySize (written to a temp file) and with timing/network-speed dependence.

symptom: After upgrading to Spring Boot 4.0.0, a repository query method annotated with a named @EntityGraph returns entities whose associations are not fetched, and serialization fails with LazyInitializationException (observed in native mode, i.e. with AOT repositories).
cause: The AOT-generated repository code looked up the named entity graph from the EntityManager but never applied it to the query (no fetchgraph hint), so the joins were missing.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Data JPA 4.0.1. Workaround until then: set spring.aot.repositories.enabled=false to restore the previous runtime-derived behavior.
notes: Reporter's package name replaced in the excerpt.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Building a chunk-oriented step that calls .retry(SomeException.class) without .retryLimit(...) fails with IllegalArgumentException "Invalid maxAttempts (-1): must be positive or zero for no retry".
cause: The builder's default retryLimit was -1, and when retryable exceptions are configured it passes that value to RetryPolicy.Builder.maxAttempts(), which rejects negative values.
fixSummary: The default retry limit was changed to 0, as in Spring Batch 5, fixed for 6.0.0-RC2. Setting retryLimit(n) explicitly avoids the exception.

symptom: With Spring Boot 4 and springdoc-openapi 3 and Spring Data REST documentation enabled, startup fails with UnsatisfiedDependencyException / TypeNotPresentException caused by ClassNotFoundException for org.springframework.boot.hateoas.autoconfigure.HateoasProperties.
cause: In Spring Boot 4 the spring-boot-starter-data-rest no longer brings spring-boot-starter-hateoas transitively, so the HATEOAS auto-configuration classes that springdoc's Data REST/HAL configuration needs are missing from the classpath. (The first exception in the thread, for Boot 4.0.0-M1, was simply that springdoc did not yet support Spring Boot 4.)

notes: Stated for 4.0.0-M2; whether later Boot 4 releases changed the starter contents is not covered by the thread.

cause: Spring Boot 4 moved the SAML2 relying party auto-configuration into the spring-boot-starter-security-saml2 starter, so adding only spring-security-saml2-service-provider no longer enables it.

appliesTo.versions: reported on JDK 21/25 (Spring Data version not stated); fixed in 3.5.11 per milestone

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Saving an aggregate whose child entity (a record in a @MappedCollection) has a static factory method named with... fails with java.lang.VerifyError in the generated <Entity>__Accessor class (on JDK 21 and 25).
cause: ClassGeneratingPropertyAccessorFactory treated the static method withExpirationDate(...) as a wither method and generated invalid bytecode for it, because it did not check whether the method is static.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Data Commons (3.5.11 per the milestone, and later lines): static with... methods are no longer considered withers.
notes: Possible workaround (not stated in the thread; inferred from the maintainer's diagnosis): avoid static methods named with... on the entity. The reporter's own workarounds (changing a field type, making the class private) were side effects. Other release lines carrying the fix are not stated.

title: @JsonValue silently ignored on a getter that is also annotated with @JsonKey
errorSample:
InvalidDefinitionException: No serializer found for class OnGetter and no properties discovered
to create BeanSerializer (to avoid exception, disable SerializationFeature.FAIL_ON_EMPTY_BEANS)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A getter annotated with both @JsonKey and @JsonValue works as a map key but serializing the object as a value fails with InvalidDefinitionException "No serializer found ... and no properties discovered". The same combination on a field works.
cause: In POJOPropertiesCollector._addGetterMethod() the annotation checks are an if/else-if chain and the @JsonKey branch returns early, so the getter is never registered as a @JsonValue accessor; _addFields() uses independent ifs.
fixSummary: Fixed in Jackson 2.23.0 so a getter with both annotations is used as both the key and the value accessor.
notes: Possible interim workaround (not stated by maintainers): put both annotations on a field, which works per the report.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A native @Query with Pageable whose FROM clause contains a subquery produces a truncated count query and an SQL syntax error (MySQL).
cause: Without JSqlParser, QueryUtils derives the count query with a regular expression that matches the first FROM, which belongs to the inner subquery, so the rest of the statement is cut off.
fixSummary: Maintainers declined to change the regex-based QueryUtils (a documented limitation). Add JSqlParser to the classpath, which the reporter confirmed fixes it, or declare an explicit countQuery on the @Query.
notes: Closed as declined by maintainers; the resolution is a documented workaround, not a code fix.

title: @DataJpaTest insert fails with H2 check constraint violation for a Boolean column with a YesNoConverter on Spring Boot 4
errorSample:
org.hibernate.exception.ConstraintViolationException: could not execute statement [Ungültige Bedingung: "CONSTRAINT_D: "
Check constraint invalid: "CONSTRAINT_D: "; SQL statement:
insert into my_entity (name,paused,version,id) values (?,?,?,?) [23514-240]] [insert into my_entity (name,paused,version,id) values (?,?,?,?)]

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: In @DataJpaTest with the embedded H2 database on Spring Boot 4.0.2, inserting an entity with a Boolean property using @Convert(converter = YesNoConverter.class) fails with ConstraintViolationException (H2 error 23514, "Check constraint invalid"). It works on Spring Boot 3.5.10.
cause: Not a Spring Data JPA problem: Hibernate generates valid DDL (paused char(1) check ((paused in ('N','Y')))) but the newer H2 shipped with Spring Boot 4 rejects the insert; a plain JDBC test with the same DDL fails identically. The reporter filed an H2 issue.
fixSummary: Workarounds from the thread: pin H2 to the version Spring Boot 3.5.10 uses (set h2.version to 2.3.232 in the build) or add @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE) so the test does not use the replaced embedded database.
notes: The exact H2 4.x version is inferred from the error code suffix [23514-240] in the stack trace; the thread does not name it. No H2 fix version is given.

title: Page<InterfaceProjection> on a derived query fails with ConverterNotFoundException (TupleImpl to Long) when the count query runs
errorSample: org.springframework.core.convert.ConverterNotFoundException: No converter found capable of converting from type [org.hibernate.sql.results.internal.TupleImpl] to type [java.lang.Long]

appliesTo.versions: reported with Spring Boot 4.0.5 and Hibernate 7.1; fixed in Spring Data JPA 4.0.5 (2025.1.5) per milestone

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A derived query method returning Page<SomeInterfaceProjection> works when the result is smaller than the page size, but throws ConverterNotFoundException (org.hibernate TupleImpl to java.lang.Long) as soon as the count query is actually executed.
cause: The interface projection was also applied to the automatically derived count query, so Hibernate returned a Tuple instead of a scalar Long.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Data JPA 4.0.5 per the issue milestone. Workaround: declare an explicit @Query with a countQuery (SELECT COUNT(x) ...).
notes: The maintainer confirmed the problem after receiving a reproducer; the fix version is taken from the milestone and the comment text does not describe the code change.
